# Green-cheeked Conure

The Green-cheeked Conure is a small, agile South American parrot with a green body, greyish chest and maroon tail. Playful and curious by reputation, it still needs daily activity, companionship and careful attention to its individual signals.

Scientific namePyrrhura molinae

Typical adult sizeAbout 25–26 cm long; around 60–80 g, with variation.

Lifetime planningOften around 20–30 years in captivity; individual lifespan varies.

## Overview and appearance

Green-cheeked Conures have green upperparts, a grey or scalloped-looking chest, maroon tail and colourful accents around the head and wings. Captive colour mutations can alter appearance, but the species retains its compact build and active nature. It is native to parts of South America, where it lives among social groups.

A small body does not mean simple care. These conures need exercise, safe chewing, foraging and daily interaction. They are capable climbers and explorers, so a bird-safe room and careful supervision matter as much as cage furnishings.

## Personality and social life

Green-cheeked Conures are often playful and curious, and many enjoy close social contact. Each bird has its own handling preferences, confidence and energy level. Nipping can occur when a bird is overstimulated, frightened or communicating a boundary; observe signals instead of assuming every approach is an invitation.

They benefit from attention balanced with independent play. A steady routine, safe toys and varied foraging can support a busy bird without requiring constant physical contact. Any introductions to other pets or birds need careful separation and supervision, never an assumption that different species will safely share space.

## Typical adult size

This small conure is typically about 25–26 cm long and around 60–80 g. Individual size and weight vary. Select an enclosure with safe bar spacing, usable room to climb and move, and enough space for varied perches and toys; provide supervised exercise outside it as well.

## Expected lifespan and long-term care

Green-cheeked Conures may live for roughly 20–30 years, although estimates differ and individual outcomes vary. Plan for a lasting relationship, ongoing care and a future guardian if needed; a small bird can still be a major life commitment.

## Talking and vocalisation

Compared with some larger conures, Green-cheeks are often described as less loud, but this is not a promise of quiet. They make calls, chatter and may learn a few sounds or words; talking ability varies. Meet the individual before deciding whether its normal voice suits your home.

## Intelligence and reward-based training

These intelligent birds can enjoy short reward-based lessons, target following and carrier practice. Add simple foraging tasks and safe objects to manipulate. Keep training upbeat and avoid punishment or forced restraint. Consistency helps a small parrot understand household routines and builds useful cooperation.

## Diet and nutrition

Offer suitable formulated food alongside a variety of fresh vegetables, with fruit and seeds used thoughtfully. A seed-only mix is not a balanced default. Ask an avian veterinarian about a specific bird’s diet and any transition, especially if it has been eating a different food; do not rely on restrictive or prescriptive online menus.

## Housing, exercise and enrichment

Provide climbing opportunities, safe perches, shreddable enrichment and supervised out-of-enclosure activity. Choose toys appropriate to a small bird and inspect cords, attachments and damaged parts. Rotate items and hide small portions of appropriate food for searching to encourage natural exploration.

## Suitability and ownership questions

A Green-cheeked Conure may suit an attentive household that can provide daily social contact, exercise and training. It can be an engaging companion, but is not a maintenance-free starter pet. Families should supervise children, respect the bird’s signals and ensure the bird has a quiet area away from busy play.

Ask about age, diet, handling preferences, vocal habits and the bird’s current routine. Prepare safe flight or exercise space and a plan for care across many years. Confirm whether an individual Green-cheeked Conure is currently available; species information is not a stock confirmation.
